reasons: Every decision input is taken from the BALROG text observation: orchestrator.py:97 reads obs['text']['long_term_context'] only, and tools/perception.py:parse_glyph_map decodes the message, language observation, cursor and map sections (map row = cursor.y-1). No env/unwrapped/nle/full_state access and no seed or task-id branching appears anywhere in orchestrator.py or tools/*.py.

tools/chart.py builds its memory only from what the agent sees and what the env refuses: terrain from drawn glyphs, visits, blocked (square, bearing) pairs recorded after a bump, and door identity from prose nouns. route() and search_plan() are BFS over that self-built chart, a legitimate planner and not an oracle lookup. The chart resets on a Dlvl change and on a system-prompt change.

The legal action set is parsed from the system prompt (tools/action_io.py:9). arbitrate() only projects the model reply onto legal verbs or falls back to the least-visited legal move, so no hardcoded action tables exist.

The model-free rungs (route, reflex, stairs, search) return LLMResponse with input_tokens=0 and output_tokens=0 and put the rung name in reasoning (orchestrator.py:66). No model was called on those steps, so this reports cost honestly and does not fabricate llm_calls. Model-called steps are labelled model:/arbiter:.

Trace spot-check over all 8 tasks: the Reasoning-column census is chart:route 1357, model:* ~694, reflex:swing 99, reflex:close-prompt 82, arbiter:least-visited 8. The rows match the code paths, and actions follow the frame (e.g. the Boxoban row-0 'cannot pass through the bars' message is followed by chart re-routing). No scorer or summary-file manipulation, and env.step is never short-circuited.
